tasks.title: Essay: Housing and Educational Opportunity
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write an essay summarising and evaluating the key points from both texts in 240–280 words. Use your own words throughout as far as possible, and include your own ideas in your answers.

promptBlocks.label: Text 1
promptBlocks.title: The case for convenience
promptBlocks.text: Student accommodation that is close to campus and affordable is often dismissed as a mere convenience, but it is in fact a precondition for educational equality. When students spend hours commuting or work multiple jobs to pay rent, their capacity to engage with academic life is severely diminished. The priority, therefore, should be to build enough housing near institutions so that no student is forced to choose between a roof and their studies. Critics who argue that this approach encourages dependency miss the point: without a stable base, the very idea of educational opportunity is hollow.

promptBlocks.label: Text 2
promptBlocks.title: The case for responsibility
promptBlocks.text: Providing convenient accommodation may solve an immediate problem, but it risks creating a culture of entitlement that undermines the resilience students need for adult life. Learning to navigate housing markets, manage budgets and make trade-offs between location and cost is itself an education. When institutions shield students from these challenges, they produce graduates who are academically qualified but practically helpless. The responsible approach is not to eliminate housing difficulties but to equip students with the skills to overcome them. Convenience today should not come at the cost of competence tomorrow.

tasks.title: Review: Student Accommodation Initiative
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: A specialist magazine for housing officers is running a series of reviews of student accommodation initiatives that aim to balance convenience with long-term responsibility. You decide to write a review of an accommodation scheme you have observed or lived in. In your review, describe the scheme and its intended balance between access and responsibility. Assess how effectively it achieved that balance, noting any unintended consequences. Recommend whether other institutions should adopt a similar model.

tasks.title: Report: Accommodation and Academic Engagement
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: You are a consultant hired by a university's student services department. The programme coordinator has asked you to write a report on how the current accommodation allocation system affects students' academic engagement and well-being. In your report, analyse the main ways in which housing location and cost influence students' ability to participate fully in academic life. Assess the potential consequences for student retention and success if these issues are not addressed. Propose two concrete actions the university could take to improve the balance between convenient access and long-term student development.

tasks.title: Article: The Right Kind of Housing Support
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: An English-language online magazine for international students is publishing a series on 'Housing and Study'. You have been contacted by an English-speaking contact who is an editor at the magazine. The editor asks you to write an article explaining your position on whether universities should prioritise providing convenient, affordable housing or focus on teaching students to manage their own accommodation. In your article, explain your position on this question. Describe one practical consequence of your preferred approach for how institutions allocate resources. Suggest how universities could implement your recommendation while still supporting students who struggle. End your article by requesting that the magazine arrange a follow-up online discussion with readers and student housing officers to explore the issue further.
